findings.title: Template registry is never loaded on metrology paths, so every hash and every threshold read is `None`
findings.description:
`_template_content_hash` calls `get_template(template_name)`, which only reads the module-level `_TEMPLATES` dict (`src/squadron/review/templates/__init__.py:155-165`). That dict is populated only by `load_all_templates()`, whose only callers are `cli/commands/review.py:304/658/756`, `pipeline/actions/review.py:111`, `pipeline/classification.py:67` and `pipeline/loader.py:174`. Nothing in `src/squadron/metrology/`, `cli/commands/metrology.py` or `cli/app.py` calls it.

In a fresh `sq metrology sample` process the registry is therefore empty and every captured sample gets `template_content_hash=None`. The existing suite pins this: `tests/metrology/test_result_ref.py:109-113` asserts `None` for `judge.slice-vs-arch`, which is a real built-in template name (`src/squadron/data/templates/judge-slice-vs-arch.yaml:1`).

What this breaks in the plan as written:
- **T7/T9:** every real cell is unversioned, so `classify_direction` can never return `GRADUATE`; `read_current_thresholds` (T7 line 122, bare `get_template`) returns `None` plus a WARNING for every cell.
- **T15/T16:** `graduate` always refuses; the "pairing meeting `GRADUATE` succeeds" test can only pass with hand-forged hashes or by test-order accident, since the registry is process-global.
- **T17 steps 3, 5, 6, 7:** all fail in a scratch repo.
- **T1:** the narrowing is a production no-op, and the "one-time re-key of historical records" (line 18) is really `None` → hash.

No task loads templates on the capture, recommend or offers paths, and no task updates `test_result_ref.py:113`, which fails the moment one does. T17 line 258 expects only the T1/T2 re-key to change existing tests.

Fix: add a task ahead of T1 that loads templates inside `_template_content_hash` and `read_current_thresholds`, updates the pinned test, and gives T2/T8/T16 a registry fixture that restores state.

findings.title: T13's result-discovery fallback makes the non-empty-offers guarantee unreachable
findings.description:
T13 (line 201) says to reuse "320's existing result-discovery surface" and, if none exists, to "scope this task to the store-recorded samples only and note the gap". No such surface exists:
- `resolve_target` globs one index only (`capture.py:93-95`).
- `_REVIEWS_SUBDIR` is private (`capture.py:37`).
- The store exposes only `list_samples` (`store.py:160`).

So the fallback is the branch that fires. A store-recorded result is by definition already sampled, so the unsampled set is always empty. That makes T13's own success line (206: "3 unsampled matching results at `rate=1.0` yields 3 `OfferTarget`s"), T14's non-empty guarantee, T16 line 247, T17 step 6 and slice criterion line 269 all unmeetable.

The task must commit to adding the reviews-directory enumeration, with a public helper or constant in `capture.py`. It must also say what the scan does with files it cannot key:
- `derive_judge_config_id` raises `MetrologyTargetError` for any review without `score` (`identity.py:252-259`), which is every non-judge review and every `.json` review in that directory.
- Deriving a `result_ref` to test "already sampled" needs `derive_project_id`, which raises `MetrologyIdentityError`. T15 line 232 limits handling to `MetrologyStoreError`/`MetrologyTargetError`, so that error would be uncaught.

findings.title: T3 and T11 together create an import cycle between `models.py` and `calibration_models.py`
findings.description:
T3 defines `GraduatedConfig` in `calibration_models.py`, which must import `JudgeConfigId` from `models.py` (directly, and via `report_models.py:13`). T11 line 175 then adds `graduated_config: GraduatedConfig | None` to `MetrologyRecord` in `models.py`, which must import `calibration_models`. A top-of-file import fails with `cannot import name 'JudgeConfigId'` from a partially initialised module.

It also pulls `squadron.pipeline.actions.judge` into every metrology import, and `squadron/pipeline/__init__.py:15-35` imports the whole pipeline package. Move `GraduatedConfig` and `EvidenceSnapshot` into `models.py`, or state the deferred-rebuild approach explicitly.

findings.title: T7's numbered precedence contradicts the behaviour it requires
findings.description:
Line 115 says to implement "exactly, in this precedence order" and step 1 is `n < floor → INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE`. Step 4 and line 121 then require a below-floor, low-match cell to return `TIGHTEN`. Followed literally, the list fails T8 line 134.

The unversioned case with a low match rate is not defined either (step 2 comes before step 4). Nor is `tighten_rate >= graduate_rate`. Rewrite the list in the order the code must evaluate: tighten check first, then floor and unversioned, then graduate, then hold. State the unversioned-and-low outcome.

findings.title: Idempotent re-graduate has no core function, and `write_graduation` cannot update in place
findings.description:
T15 line 230 requires "update its evidence snapshot in place … one record, not two". T11 provides only `write_graduation`, which "returns a generated record id" (line 176), and `find_graduation`, which returns a `GraduatedConfig` with no record id or path (line 177). Nothing can locate the file to overwrite, so the update logic lands in the Typer shell, against line 228's "thin shells".

A killed delete-then-write, or two generated ids, leaves two records for one identity; `find_graduation` has no rule for that. Specify a deterministic record id derived from `(JudgeConfigId, artifact_level)` so a re-write overwrites atomically through `_write_atomic`.

T11 is also ambiguous about whether these are module functions taking `store` or `MetrologyStore` methods; lines 176-178 say both.

findings.title: `graduate` assumes one cell per `(template, model, level)`, but agreement groups on the hash
Graduation records have no project scope and no removal command
findings.description:
The store is user-level and cross-project (`~/.config/squadron/metrology`). `GraduatedConfig` carries no project id (T3 line 64), and `list_graduations` / `select_residual_offers` take no project filter. `offers --project ID` (line 231) therefore has nothing to filter on.

T13 line 203 defines lapse as "no longer matches any current judge result". Running `offers` in any other repo then reports every graduation as lapsed due to a config change, which is false.

No command in the plan removes or supersedes a graduation. After a prompt edit and re-graduation, the stale record stays and prints its lapse line on every `offers` run until someone deletes the JSON file by hand.

findings.title: Float config keys are not settable through `sq config set`, and defaults are unspecified
findings.description:
`_coerce_value` handles only `int` and `str` and raises `ValueError("Unsupported config type")` otherwise. `config_set` catches only `KeyError` (`cli/commands/config.py:33-37`). After T5, `sq config set metrology.graduate_match_rate 0.9` ends in a traceback. T6 hides this because it writes `.squadron.toml` directly.

Related gaps in T5/T6:
- **Defaults:** T5 gives no default values, yet T6 line 104 asserts "correct … defaults".
- **Wrong claim:** T5's success line says `sq config list` shows descriptions; it prints name, value and source only (`config.py:92`).
- **Validated readers:** T15 reads three rates and the floor with none specified. The existing floor reader is private (`report.py:189`), and a TOML `1` reads back as `int`.

findings.title: Malformed `judge:` block is claimed covered but is neither handled nor tested
findings.description:
`resolve_thresholds` calls `float()` on the raw value and raises `ValueError`/`TypeError` on a non-numeric floor. The pipeline catches this itself (`pipeline/actions/review.py:230-238`).

T7's `read_current_thresholds` has no such handling. The error escapes `recommend_thresholds` and the CLI, which catches only the two metrology errors.

The slice's failure-mode row (line 242) requires a flagged target, a WARNING and a test. Line 287 of the task file says this is "inherited from `resolve_thresholds`, exercised in T8", but T8 (lines 131-137) has no such case and there is nothing to inherit.

findings.title: Runtime-drawn-model limitation is not in the note and not asserted
findings.description:
Slice criterion line 270 requires the runtime-drawn-model limitation to be "stated where the recommendation is produced (asserted: the note is present in output, including `--json`)". Slice line 201 specifies that the note says the threshold cannot track a pool-drawn model.

T9 line 147 covers only the template-and-model pairing sentence. T10 line 161 and T16 line 243 assert only that the note is non-empty or present. Add the limitation text to T9 and a content assertion on text and `--json` output.

findings.title: T17 step 5 passes with or without T1
findings.description:
Agreement cells are grouped on each sample's stored `judge_config`. Editing `judge.pass_floor` or `system_prompt` and re-running `report agreement` (line 265) shows identical cells and n before and after T1. The `system_prompt` half ("new `JudgeConfigId`, evidence separates") can never be observed that way.

The regression only shows when a new sample is captured after each edit: it should join the existing cell after a threshold edit and open a new cell after a prompt edit. Add those captures to step 5.

The walkthrough T17 defers to also uses `--template judge-tasks-vs-slice` (slice line 312). The template's name is `judge.tasks-vs-slice` (`src/squadron/data/templates/judge-tasks-vs-slice.yaml:1`), so that command finds no cell.

findings.title: T13 pins a return type that cannot carry the lapse or pruned signals T14 asserts
findings.description:
The signature is fixed as `-> list[OfferTarget]`. Line 203 leaves the lapse signal open ("return enough information (or have the CLI re-derive it…)"), and T14 line 217 asserts "on whatever signal T13 produces".

T14 line 218 tests a pruned review file that is "skipped, counted … WARNING logged". T13 has no pruned-file step and no place for a count. `GraduatedConfig` references no review paths, so a deleted file is simply absent from a scan.

Define one result shape, for example per-graduation offers, status (active, exhausted or lapsed) and skipped count. State where a pruned path can come from.

findings.title: Commit markers follow all 17 tasks, including implementation before its tests
findings.description:
Every task ends in a `**Commit:**` line (39, 52, 69, … 272). Eight of them land implementation before the test task that verifies it (T1, T3, T5, T7, T9, T11, T13, T15). Put one marker per implementation-and-test pair, eight or nine in total.

T10's no-mutation check (line 163) can be cut. `recommend_thresholds` takes no store or cwd, and T16 line 248 already makes the assertion the slice asks for at the `recommend` entry point.

findings.title: Signatures deviate from the slice design without saying so
findings.description:
- `classify_direction` gains `versioned`, `graduate_rate` and `tighten_rate` (slice line 84 has three parameters).
- `recommend_thresholds` drops `current: ThresholdSnapshot` (slice line 83).
- `read_current_thresholds` and `ThresholdTarget.current` become optional (slice lines 85, 98).

All are sound and needed by the failure-mode table; `ThresholdSnapshot` is undefined in the design. A one-line note in the Context Summary would stop an implementer "correcting" them back.

findings.title: `recommend --json` with `--level` is unspecified
findings.description: The existing `report agreement` filters rows by level but emits the unfiltered model under `--json`. T15 line 229 does not say which behaviour `recommend` follows.
